the most important and most interesting result of our MOST observations of the M67 field is that we have been able to confirm the existence of the blue straggler binary ES Cnc and to show that the system consists of two stars with masses of about 1.5 and 0.2 M ⊙. This result is of fundamental importance, as it shows that blue straggler stars can be formed by mass transfer and not only by stellar collisions.

the MOST satellite photometry of selected variable stars in the M-67 field, covering nearly continuously about 10 days in year 2004 and about 30 days in year 2011, has led to the detection of new eclipsing binaries and the confirmation of the existence of the blue-straggling binary/triple systems AH Cnc, ES CNC and EV Cnc, and the δ Scuti pulsating stars EX Cnc and EW Cnc.

the most likely cause for the observed light curve of AH Cnc is a combination of a dark spot on one of the stars and an eccentric orbit, and that the spot is not on the surface of the secondary star, as suggested by the light curve of the eclipses, but on the surface of a third, fainter star in a hierarchical triple system.
